title: No rule holds the section that states the command surface
foundBy: user report: "The section also never gained orientation, added around the same time"
stint: 2026-09-10 session: close the two gaps LNT-002 left

evidence.verified: go test ./internal/surface/ -count=1: TestSurfaceSectionMissingAVerbIsReported, TestCompleteSurfaceSectionIsNotReported and TestSurfaceSectionSkipsWhenNotConfigured PASS. Against the built binary on codesweep-ai/campaign with `surfaceSection: SPEC.md#3.1`, dropping `orientation` from the 3.1 block reports `SURF-105 error SPEC.md#3.1 states the command surface and does not name 1 verb(s) the binary carries: orientation [SPEC.md:99]`, where it reported 0 errors before. On this repository with `surfaceSection: MANUAL.md#Synopsis`, dropping `cs-lint oss` from the synopsis reports SURF-105 naming `oss`. make check passes.

resolution: SURF-105 reads the fenced blocks under a nominated section and reports every top-level verb the binary carries that the section does not name. The section is named by `docs.surface.surfaceSection` as `DOC.md#heading`, because which section claims the surface is this project's knowledge rather than the linter's. A repository that nominates none gets a named skip, per R65. SPEC.md R66 states the requirement.
details:
SURF-102 matches each verb as a whole word against the whole document set flattened into one string, so no section is accountable for the surface it announces.

Measured on `codesweep-ai/campaign`: deleting `orientation` from the SPEC.md 3.1 synopsis reports 0 errors, because `orientation` still appears 13 times in MANUAL.md and 8 in PLAYBOOK.md. The section announces itself as "the host command surface" and can lose a verb in silence.

The match is also prose rather than surface. `wholeWord(last).MatchString(prose)` is satisfied by any use of the word. `orientation` is an ordinary English noun and a glossary term in that project, so SURF-102 would stay quiet even if no page named the command.

LNT-002's closing note claims SURF-102 covers this case from the other side. That is wrong, and this record corrects it.

The gap is why `campaign` carried `internal/cli/manual_test.go:TestSpecNamesEveryCommand`, a Go test holding the block against its own command tree. Its comment names both drifts: `pin` outliving its removal by six months, and `orientation` never arriving. That is a workaround one project can afford and every other would have to rewrite for itself.
